# SAFT-VR-Mie flash

`eos.tp_flash_saft`

## Source

**Lafitte, T. et al. (2013)**

NeqSim's own flash for this family: Wilson K-values to seed, successive substitution with Rachford-Rice inside, and each phase's fugacity coefficients from a separate single-phase solve.

DOI: [10.1063/1.4819786](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4819786)


## Algorithm

A model rather than a calculation: what this page pins down is the procedure,
not an equation, and both implementations read it from here.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Scheme | `successive_substitution_flash` |
| Convergence | `relative` |
| Tolerance | `1e-05` |
| Max iterations | `50` |
| Initialisation | `wilson` |

## Inner procedure

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Scheme | `rachford_rice_bisection` |
| Convergence | `absolute` |
| Tolerance | `1e-14` |
| Max iterations | `200` |

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `components` | - | the substances the mixture is made of, by name, resolved against the component databank with their SAFT-VR-Mie set and the cubic constants the seed is built from |
| `T` | K | absolute temperature |
| `P` | Pa | absolute pressure |
| `z` | dimensionless | the feed's mole fractions, checked rather than renormalised |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `beta` | dimensionless | *Optional.* the vapour fraction, present only when the flash found a split. A single-phase answer has no vapour fraction rather than a zero one. |
| `x` | dimensionless | liquid-phase mole fractions, the feed itself when there is one phase |
| `y` | dimensionless | vapour-phase mole fractions, the feed itself when there is one phase |
| `k` | dimensionless | K-values, `K_i = phi_i^L / phi_i^V`, the iterate the loop converges on |
| `ln_phi_liquid` | dimensionless | fugacity coefficients in the liquid phase, as logarithms |
| `ln_phi_vapour` | dimensionless | fugacity coefficients in the vapour phase, as logarithms |
| `z_liquid` | dimensionless | the compressibility factor of the liquid solve |
| `z_vapour` | dimensionless | the compressibility factor of the vapour solve |
| `phase` | two_phase / all_liquid / all_vapour / trivial | what the converged state is. `all_liquid` and `all_vapour` are the Gibbs comparison's two answers, and `trivial` is not reachable here: a loop that stops on its bound reports one phase by the comparison rather than by a trivial solution. |
| `iterations` | dimensionless | successive-substitution steps taken |
| `residual` | dimensionless | the largest relative change in a K-value at the last step |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `T > 0` | raises | an absolute temperature; zero and below are not states |
| `P > 0` | raises | an absolute pressure; zero and below are not states |

## Assumptions

- **it is a different algorithm from every other flash here, and that is the model.** NeqSim dispatches a `SystemSAFTVRMie` to `TPflashSAFT` by `instanceof`, and that class reaches its K-values by successive substitution rather than by the Newton scheme the generic `TPflash` uses.
- the seed is Wilson's, `exp(ln(Pc/P) + 5.373 (1 + omega)(1 - Tc/T))`, from the **cubic** constants beside the Mie set. It is a ratio of pressures, so it is unit-free.
- each phase's fugacity coefficients come from a single-phase solve at that trial composition, on that side - which is what NeqSim does by building a fresh system per call, and what makes this model's cost a volume solve per phase per iteration.
- **the loop stops at a relative K change of `1e-5` where NeqSim stops at `1e-6`**: the K-values carry this model's central differences and their noise floor is about `2e-6`. The threshold decides which branch is taken, so one below that floor is a different answer, not a stricter test.
- a vapour fraction outside `(1e-10, 1 - 1e-10)` is **a branch, not a failure**: the model reports a single phase and picks between gas and liquid by comparing `sum_i x_i ln phi_i` on the two roots. The ideal part is identical in both, so that is the whole of the Gibbs comparison.
- the chain term's contact value is guarded to the Carnahan-Starling one outside a packing fraction of `(1e-10, 0.7)`, as `calcGMieBlended` is: the quartic it would otherwise evaluate carries `ln(1 - eta)`, which past one is not a number. A flash's trial compositions walk through that region.
- **no association term**, for the reason `eos.saft_vr_mie_phase` records. A fluid whose components carry sites is refused rather than given an association computed over nothing.
- the two phases are assumed to be at the same temperature and pressure as the feed - a flash, not a rigorous column stage. Nothing here does an energy balance.
